MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  APRIL 29, 2020

Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this meeting was held via teleconference.

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Schmitz, Addleman, Arata, Bayer,
  Buresh, Carman, Carrese, Friedman,
  Medawar, Seamans, Stegura, Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Shinn, Silvano

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  JANUARY 30, 2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE CORMAN to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  JANUARY 30, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  SAFETY ELEMENT
John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International (MBI), stated that at the last meeting, the
question was asked whether to include pandemics in the Safety Element. At the time, the
Cornovirus was beginning to get some press and now it is at the forefront of everyone’s mind. Mr.
Bellas stated that his team and city staff have discussed and crafted policies which will be
introduced as a first order of business.

Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, MBI, introduced the new policies related to pandemics.

Per the request of Chair Schmitz, Administrative Analyst Slawson, provided an update on the
city’s Emergency Operations Plan. She stated that the Emergency Operations Plan is a response
plan. The Coronavirus unfolded during the time that the Emergency Operations Plan was being
developed and did not include a global pandemic. An after action plan will be developed in order
to incorporate into the Emergency Operations Plan.

GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
MINUTES, APRIL 29, 2020
 Committee Member Stegura stated that the city should be commended for all of the information
on the status of things during this times and thanked the city for the information being sent by e-
mail and through social media outlets.

Chair Schmitz added that staff has put in place creative and innovative ways to communicate
information. Some of which has been learned in this health crisis have been good practices, but
do not yet know if they are best practices and asked how detailed the protocol need to be within
the Safety Element.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that for the purpose of including it in the Safety Element, the bullet below
would be included as written. For implementation and when it is moved to the Emergency
Operations plan it could be updated as more is learned about best practices.

The committee agreed to include the following policy with the change as noted:

  •  New Policy: Include operations protocol for public health crisis scenarios in City’s
  Operation Plan.

In response to a question by CHAIR SCHMITZ, Administrative Analyst Slawson stated that there
already protocols in place for agencies to inform the city in case of earthquakes and fires. In the
case of a health crisis, the city would take direction from the Health Department.

The committee agreed to include the following policy:

  •  New Policy: Future preparedness/response planning efforts should be informed by
  applicable scientific research and modelling by responsible agencies and organizations.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented on the following policy and suggested that
the City services be defined.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE suggested that health crisis should be more specific.

In response to a question by CHAIR SCHMITZ, CITY MANAGER GRAMMER stated that during
this health crisis, staff has endeavored to make all essential City services available to the public.
From staffs perspective, staff has a sense of what those essential services are.

Ms. Barbhaya added that the services that can be provided during this health crisis may not be
possible during a different health crisis. She suggested to change the following statement to, “…
essential City services as directed by the State”.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER suggested inserting the word, “timely”, and commended the City
on the efforts made in responding to the current health crisis from the very beginning.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS stated that the policies should remain broad since, for
example, this current health crisis changes from day to day.

CITY MANAGER GRAMMER suggested adding “public” health crisis.

The committee agreed to include the following policy with the changes as noted:

  •  New Policy: To the extent possible keep Ensure essential City services remain
  operational and timely in the event of public health crisis scenarios.

CHAIR SCHMITZ expressed her concern with the specificity in analyzing the COVID-19 situation
since it should be best practice to do this after every crisis.

The committee members held a brief discussion and agreed that including COVID-19 in the policy
would be too specific.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that the following policy will be moved to an implementation measure.

The committee agreed to include the following policy with the changes as noted:

GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
MINUTES, APRIL 29, 2020
   •  New Policy: After each declared emergency analyze the City’s response through to
  the COVID-19 situation to informed future health crisis preparedness and future
  responses.

After a brief discussion, the committee members agreed to remove the following policy since it is
understood that the dissmemination of information would be done in coordination with federal,
state, county agencies, and other jurisdictions.

  •  New Policy: Coordinate with federal, state, county agencies, and neighboring jurisdictions
  to disseminate information regarding health threats and its containment.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated if the city wanted to do something out of the
ordinary, then this would help to provide guidance in developing procedures.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA expressed her concern with how the residents would interpret
this policy when there is a conflict between government agencies.
Mr. Bellas explained that this policy is not meant for individual citizens and rather for the city to
formulate its response in disseminating information.

Administrative Analyst Slawson provided information on the levels of government on the recovery
side. When an emergency is declared and you seek to the levels of government financial
assistance, then the city will be following their direction and guidance.

City Manager Grammer stated that this policy is helpful to the city in making decisions but is also
helpful to inform residents on why the city is making certain decisions.

The committee agreed to include the following policy with the change noted:

  •  New Policy: In the event of federal, state, or and local health emergency declarations,
  follow the direction and guidance of appropriate public health and infrastructure agencies.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN inquired about an earlier policy which includes having supplies
for employees for three days.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that the earlier policy was referring to supplies for all employees and this
policy covers protective equipment for essential employees.

Mr. Bellas stated that the following policy was intended to indicate that the city’s policy is that, if
employees are working, they have what they need at that time.

CHAIR SCHMITZ expressed her concern with combining the two policies and stated that this
policy seems more pertinent to the current situation. If the city has essential services and staff is
coming in, then to the extent possible, the city is providing staff with protective equipment.

The committee agreed to include the following policy wth the correction noted:

  •  New Policy: In the event of a public health emergency, to the extent available, ensure that
  City employees have access to appropriate protective equipment in order to provide
  essential services.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN expressed his concern with adding this policy since this is a
thirty year plan and there will be changes in technology.

CHAIR SCHMITZ suggested that if the city is going to invest in infrastructure, then think about its
mobility.

The committee agreed to move this policy as an implementation strategy with the changes noted:

  •  New Policy: When investing in city work place infrastructure planning for and/or
  purchasing computer hardware and software, information systems/technology, and other
  workspace consider the usability in telecommuting conditions and physical distancing
  scenarios.

GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
MINUTES, APRIL 29, 2020
 Ms. Barbhaya stated that at the last meeting, there was discussion about combining the following
policies and suggested, “Educate city officials and staff on a regular basis regarding established
procedures for decision making in the event of a disaster.”

After a brief discussion, the committee agreed to keep Policy 4.1., make 4.2 an implementation
strategy, and delete 4.4.

    Policy 4.1 Provide City officials with a basis protocols for disaster preparedness decision
  making and establish a public education program for disaster preparedness.

    Policy 4.2 Establish a line of command to ensure that the decision making process will
  function satisfactorily in the event of a major disaster.

    Policy 4.4 Encourage cooperation among adjacent communities to provide back-up law
  enforcement assistance in emergency situations.

Ms. Barhbhaya recommended combining Policies 5.1 and 5.2 as follows, “Support the Los
Angeles County’s Sheriff’s Department in crime prevention and law enforcement to make sure
there are adequate resources to meet the needs of the community.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR suggested including, …work with the contracted law
enforcement agency.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER suggested changing support to working with the Sheriff’s
Department.

The committee agreed to include Policy 5.1, move Policy 5.2 as an implementation measure, and
delete Policy 5.3.

    Policy 5.1 Work with, and support the contracted law enforcement agency Sheriff’s
  Department in crime prevention and law enforcement efforts, to make sure there are
  adequate resources to meet the needs of the community.
    Policy 5.2 Collaborate Cooperate with neighboring jurisdictions cities, Los Angeles
  County, California State and U.S. Federal agencies in crime prevention and law
  enforcement.
    Policy 5.3 Evaluate the incidence of crime and develop measures needed to deter crime
  or apprehend criminals.
Ms. Barbhaya recommended combining policies 6.1 and 6.2 as follows, “Cooperate with
responsible federal, state and local county agencies to minimize the risk to the community from
the use, transportation and storage of hazardous materials.”
COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN suggested including the removal of hazardous materials in
case of a spill or hazardous materials found that require removal.
A discussion ensued.
City Manager Grammer stated that there may be language that can used from the stormwater
permit application. CHAIR SCHMITZ added that the language be reviewed in order to not
introduce liability to the city on the MS4 permit.
The committee agreed to bring this policy back at a later time for revisions.
    Policy 6.1 Restrict the travel of vehicles carrying hazardous material through the City.
    Policy 6.2 Monitor and limit the use and production of hazardous materials by businesses
  and industries in the City.
Ms. Barbhaya inquired, in reference to the following policy, if there are any structures in the city
that do not meet seismic safety standards.
Director Wahba recommended removing this policy since residential properties built after the 50’s
are all bolted, however, may not meet current requirements. There are no unreinforced brick
buildings in the city.

GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
MINUTES, APRIL 29, 2020
 Planning Manager added the critical and semi-critical does not refer to all properties and rather
to places like City Hall, Schools and Hospitals.
The committee agreed to remove the following policies:
    Policy 1.1 Ensure that existing critical and semi-critical structures throughout the City meet
  seismic safety standards within ten years and that new facilities are developed to
  upgraded standards.
    Policy 1.6 Enforce seismic design provisions for Seismic Zone 4 of the Uniform Building
  Code to ensure adequate review and inspection to ensure that stairways and elevators
  are adequately strengthened and nonstructural components such as emergency
  generators, water beaters, computers, and cabinets are securely anchored in critical
  facilities.
The committee agreed to review this policy and bring it back:
    Policy 1.7 Require fault investigations along traces of the Palos Verdes and Cabrillo faults
  to comply with guidelines implemented by the Alquist-Priolo special Studies Zone Act.
  Buildings for human occupancy should be setback a minimum of 50 feet from those faults
  that are shown to be active or from fault traces where the risk cannot be determined.
Ms. Barbhaya recommended changing policy 2.3 as follow,”Periodically update site design and
maintenance standards to include best practices and innovative technologies/materials for new
development and major renovations in areas with high fire hazard or soil erosion potential.
After a brief discussion, the recommended that the following policy will be revised and brough
back to the committee for review:
    Policy 2.3 Develop stringent site design and maintenance standards or areas with high
  fire hazard or soil erosion potential.
The committee agreed to remove the following policy:
    Policy 2.4 Regularly review technical data on public safety and seismic safety for use in
  the decision-making process.
Ms. Barbhaya recommended and the committee agreed to change Policy 3.3 as follows:
Ensure that the city maintains a current emergency supply for all its employees for a three day
period
    Policy 3.3 Ensure that adequate provisions are made to supply drinking water for extended
  periods of time in the event of a major disaster.
The committee agreed to remove the following policy:
    Policy 3.4 Develop procedures to follow in the event of flooding, erosion, and possible
  reservoir failure and investigate ways of reducing the likelihood of their occurrence.
CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the consultants for allowing this platform to hold this meeting and for
all committee members for their participation.
6.  CONSULTANT/STAFF/COMMITTEE ITEMS

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 7:51 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,

_________________________________  _____________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Velveth Schmitz, Chair

GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
MINUTES, APRIL 29, 2020
